data_evidence.shift_location_note: Yes, dawn and afternoon trips start in different places. Dawn trips (start 04-06h, n=1250 of 3430 multi-bin trips) open in Rio Maior town: top first-stop cells 39.33719,-8.93518 (n=158) and 39.33451,-8.93167 (n=118), with 43.0% of first stops within 2 km of the Estaleiro Municipal (39.33921,-8.92493). Afternoon trips (start 14-15h, n=1944) most often open in the southern parishes: top cell 39.26219,-8.83352 (Sao Joao da Ribeira/Marmeleira area, n=142), then 39.25639,-8.89603 (n=84); only 25.9% start within 2 km of the estaleiro (median first-stop distance 6.1 km vs 4.9 km for dawn trips). This fits a single town-side depot with afternoon routes deadheading out to peripheral parishes before the first recorded container stop. Note stops are container locations only - the depot visit and the tipping leg are not themselves recorded, so first/last hot cells are depot-side hints, not the depot itself.

notes: OSM scan of Geofabrik portugal-latest (bbox lon -9.5..-8.3, lat 38.9..39.7; layers pois, pois_a, landuse_a, traffic) kept fclass recycling/landfill/waste_transfer_station or waste keywords in name; 612 features after dedupe. ~570 were street ecopontos/supermarket bring-banks or unnamed distant polygons and were excluded from the inventory. Rio Maior belonged to Resioeste, absorbed by Valorsul in 2010, so its urban and selective waste flows through the Valorsul (Oeste) system, not the Santarém-district systems (Ecoparque do Relvão/Resitejo, Ecolezíria), which are listed only as geographic candidates.
synthesis: Rio Maior's recyclables almost certainly funnel through the co-located Valorsul pair in the Zona Industrial just south-east of town: the Estação de Transferência (approx 39.3196,-8.9240) and the Ecocentro de Rio Maior (39.3174,-8.9108), 2.3-2.8 km from the town-centre depot area - the only licensed tipping points inside the municipality. From the transfer station, compacted selective-collection loads are hauled by Valorsul to the CTRO sorting centre at Vilar, Cadaval (39.186,-9.145, ~28 km by road), the Oeste region's triagem plant co-located with the Aterro Sanitário do Oeste, while undifferentiated waste goes to the CTRSU/incinerator at São João da Talha with the Mato da Cruz landfill as backup. The truck GPS evidence (first/last stop hot cells clustering around the Estaleiro Municipal and the Zona Industrial) is consistent with collection rounds ending at the transfer station, with the long-haul leg to Cadaval or Lisbon handled by Valorsul's own transport, not the municipal fleet. Other named sites within 15 km are unnamed old landfill polygons and the ETAR - none plausible recyclables destinations - and the nearest non-Valorsul alternatives (Ecocentro de Santarém, Ecocentro do Cartaxo, private operators at Azambuja/Alcanena/Chamusca) all lie 20+ km away in other systems' service areas.
